QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_25

question.text: RVPI (Residual Value to Paid-In) of a fund measures:

answer.text: Cumulative cash distributions divided by paid-in capital
The remaining market/fair value of unrealised investments divided by paid-in capital
The management fee accrued but not paid

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.7.4.3: RVPI = AUM (unrealised residual value) / Total Capital Contributions. It captures the paper value still in the fund. Early in life, RVPI dominates; late in life, it trends to zero. **The Trap:** Option A is DPI. Option C is mathematically wrong. Option D is fee concept. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B tests RVPI; XXI-B covers it for PMS illiquid sleeves. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** RVPI is only as reliable as your valuation policy. Ensure your valuation methodology (Cat I/II) is documented and third-party-reviewed — SEBI mandates independent valuations for AIFs and LP disputes over RVPI write-downs are common.
